operator.name: National Center for O*NET Development; sponsored by US Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration (USDOL/ETA)

capabilities: Official versioned JSON export of 1,016 US occupation codes, titles and complete short occupation descriptions; anonymous local metadata/description search without account or key.
Twenty distinct English role-title queries and native IDs span all 20 industry tags; each sector is sampled, not exhaustively covered.
Exact O*NET-SOC code and all-word title/title-plus-description matching. No semantic task inference, salary lookup, vacancies, full training manuals, translation or India-local equivalence.

query.identity: release + O*NET-SOC code; current OnLine page can change independently of the pinned metadata release
query.matching: NFKC/casefold whole words, all terms required; simple terminal-s singular/plural matching for terms longer than three characters. No synonyms, task inference or stemming.
query.subset: Only occupation_data: code, English title and full short description. Other O*NET tables, job-ad feeds and website enrichment excluded.

licensing: O*NET 31.0 downloadable database content is CC BY 4.0. Credit USDOL/ETA, include version and license link, indicate changes and observe O*NET trademark/nonendorsement wording. Career exploration tools and other site content have separate licenses.
limitations: US taxonomy and English descriptions only. Managed-cloud access was observed; USA/India reader network availability was not independently tested.
One catalog overlaps 20 industry tags; one role sample per tag does not meet any 100-origin target or establish broad task/training coverage.
31.0 distribution has an occupation table unchanged since 25.1 per dictionary; current OnLine page update labels cover richer data and do not re-date the pinned descriptions.
Literal term search can miss synonymous occupations: agriculture misses Farmers; logistics misses Logisticians. Code/title queries remain supported.
30.3 JSON URL reports a 30.4 dictionary internally and is rejected as a 30.3 release. Published 30.3 spreadsheet rows match 31.0; mismatch remains an open provider-evidence discrepancy.
Numeric download quota is not published in the reviewed docs; no unlimited-service claim. No API key/account, paid service or automatic refresh was configured.
next_action: Resolve or explicitly retire the archived JSON/version discrepancy on new official evidence; retain failed observations. Assign accountable runtime refresh ownership before integration. Continue independent catalog/entity and India/language gaps; no runtime import or activation.

observed_previous_release.interpretation: Metadata rows compared from separately published release files. No removed IDs is not an observed deletion. The JSON 30.3 URL internal dictionary says 30.4; that discrepancy remains unresolved and the JSON was not accepted as a 30.3 inventory.

facts.schema_guards: Reject wrong dictionary/table/version, duplicate/malformed IDs, missing titles/descriptions, truncation or changed pinned hash/count.

facts.failure_fixture_scope: Research probe fixtures: HTTP429, HTTP503, transport failure status null and truncated HTTP200 produce unverified observations with no results; one attempt and no automatic retry. This is fail-stop/manual revisit, not an automatic runtime retry scheduler.

analysis_refs.heading: Group and tagging model
analysis_refs.text:
Use `industryIds`, source-supplied occupation codes/titles, `taskTerms`, content
kind, language, jurisdiction, publication/version date and equipment/process
context. Keep locally supplied occupation labels; do not automatically equate
different countries' qualifications. The [O*NET database](https://www.onetcenter.org/database.html)
and its [documented API](https://services.onetcenter.org/reference/start/overview)
can supply US role/task vocabulary. India's [National Classification of
Occupations](https://www.dge.gov.in/national_classification_of_occupations) supplies
another classification. Neither is a universal collection of practical manuals.

analysis_refs.heading: Category-specific acceptance and evidence
analysis_refs.text:
Before enablement, prove item-level topic/title retrieval and stable resolution,
free full-item access, source permissions and refresh behavior under the shared
review template. Neither an O*NET occupational match nor an NQR qualification
match establishes that another provider has the requested manual. Identifier-only
resolvers support discovery but do not count toward searchable-origin targets.

analysis_refs.heading: Documentation review limits
analysis_refs.text:
This review inspected primary web documentation/catalog pages, not production
API requests or a hundred sources per industry. O*NET explicitly documents an
API and downloadable data; reuse that as vocabulary evidence only until the
chosen integration is tested. The NQR migration notice was observed directly.
FDA/FAA/OSHA/NIST, ROSA P, FAO/WHO/IMO and Bharat Skills pages were readable.
India's ICAR, MSME, FSSAI, NHM and CERT-In discovery links also appeared in official
search results; catalog/permissions checks remain necessary.
